stem: Two rooms have the same RH, but one room is substantially warmer. Why should a technician avoid assuming their atmospheric demand is identical?
choices: Temperature changes vapor-pressure relationships, so the same RH can represent different drying demand
RH has no relationship to plant environment
Warm air always means the crop needs more fertilizer
The cooler room has no measurable water demand
rationale: Relative humidity is temperature-dependent. Similar RH at different temperatures does not necessarily represent the same vapor-pressure environment.
